# MCPJam API

> Programmatic access to the MCP servers in y

our MCPJam projects: diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API
is in preview.** It works today and we use it ourselves, but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surface may change, i
ncluding in\n> breaking ways, while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on this page, build
a [tolerant\n> reader](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord](https://discord

.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or
> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com

/settings/api-keys)
>
> Go straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,
> you'll be asked to sign in and

then land right back on the API keys page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your
[hosted](https://doc

s.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) projects (from CI, scripts, or your own agents)
without opening the UI.

What you can do with

it today:

* **Discover your resources**: list your projects, their servers, eval
 suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the

other routes need is
 self-serve
* **Validate a server**: connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot
* **Run the d
octor**: the probe → connect → initialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements**: does this server need an OAuth
grant?\n* **List tools, prompts, and resources**: the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt**: execute primit
ives and get the MCP result back verbatim\n* **Read a resource** by URI\n* **Export a full snapshot**: tools, resources, and promp
ts as one JSON document\n* **Manage a project's clients**: list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template like `claude`/`chat
gpt`/`cursor`, or from a full config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that define how\n MCPJam
connects to and talks to your MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId` back as `expec
tedConfigId` for a\n config change and its `name` back as `expectedName` for a rename (a rename\n does not rotate the config, so
the config token cannot detect a concurrent\n one), and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently reverted\n* **Manage
a project's environments**: list, read, and archive the named\n execution bundles (host + optional server group) that eval\n sui
tes and goals run against,\n and **preview** what one resolves to before launching it\n* **List a project's studies**: name, acce
ss mode, attached servers, and\n share link, and **read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,\n tool-approval policy, an
d resolved servers\n* **Author eval suites**: create a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, test cases) synchronously and
get a `suiteId` back; no run is started and no credits are spent\n* **Run eval suites asynchronously**: create a run from a saved
suite, get a `202` + `runId`\n immediately, then poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, token\n usage, latency), and f
ull traces. Runs appear live in the hosted UI,\n tagged `source: \"api\"`\n* **Manage a server's accounts**: complete OAuth yours
elf (e.g. the SDK's\n `runOAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n account; list, rename, choose
the default, and delete accounts. Tokens are\n write-only: no route returns one\n* **Run a headless agent turn**: send a message
history, get back the\n assistant reply, the platform operations it invoked, references to any\n resources it created (eval sui
tes), and token usage; the model is pinned\n server-side and billed to the project\n* **Send feedback**: report a bug, a missing
capability, or something\n confusing to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the\n `send_feedback` MCP to

ol calls

All endpoints operate on servers you have already added to a project in the
hosted inspector. Managing API keys remai

ns UI-only; see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https:/

/app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.

## Authe
curl -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Beare

r $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings →
API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)\n in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there\n
directly).\n2. Click **Create API key**, name it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediat

ely; **it is shown exactly once** and never
 stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at

any time. Revocation takes effect
immediately.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **
as you,\ninside that organization**. Per-request authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access

that project and server. A key
can never reach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions

while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface
> with an `sk_…` bearer f
ail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in\n> the UI.\n> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create key

s.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager; never
commit it to\n source control or ship it in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can
tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke

it immediately in
 [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `d
etails.reason: \"ORPHANED_KEY\"`, the key\nis no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used; create a new key\nfrom [Setti

ngs](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON bo
dy (most accept\nan empty `{}`). **Reads**, the catalog listings and eval-run polling, are\n`GET` and take their options (`cursor`

, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | -
|\n| Single resource | The resource object directly |\n| Collection | `{ \"items\": [...], \"nextCursor\": \"...\" }`; `nextCurso
r` omitted on the last page |\n| Error | `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a matching HTTP st

atus |

**Pagination.** Collections are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's
`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next request

(body field on `POST` lists,
query parameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque; don't parse them.

**Authoring vs running su
ites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201` with th
e\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything; author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it validates and crea
tes a run synchronously, then\ndetaches execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}` until `status`

is `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, or `timed_out`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable through the AP
